speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I understand you've had a tympanoplasty and are now experiencing occasional shooting ear pain and difficulty wearing earrings. To help me understand your current condition, can you describe exactly where you feel the pain and what triggers it?

speaker: Patient
text: 25-year-old female. The patient has a history of polycystic ovarian syndrome, depression, and chronic bilateral ear infections. She underwent right ear tympanoplasty 12 weeks ago. Although audiology report from one week ago showed improved hearing by 20 decibels, she reports occasional shooting pain when eating and discomfort when wearing earrings. She describes her job as stressful and mentions poor sleep quality.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Persistent Oticgia (Shooting Ear Pain) secondary to Trigeminal Neuralgia of the Mandibular Branch (V3) and/or Otic Capsular Neuralgia (Neuropathic Pain) following Tympanoplasty.

I have noted your history of PCOS, depression, and chronic ear infections, as well as the successful hearing improvement post-surgery. However, the specific symptom of "shooting pain when eating" combined with pain from earrings suggests a neuropathic component or a structural issue like a foreign body or granulation tissue irritating the auriculotemporal nerve. Given your history of chronic ear infections, we must also rule out a recurrent cholesteatoma or an ossicular chain issue causing referred pain.
